title: A Powerful Quake Shakes Panama, Leaving Dozens Injured and Infrastructure Crippled
deck: A 7.7-magnitude tremor struck southern Panama, prompting a national disaster declaration, widespread power outages, and damage to hundreds of buildings, while a separate 7.2-magnitude shock earlier in the week left 27 people injured.
paragraphs: In October, a massive earthquake rattled southern Panama. Measured at 7.7 on the Richter scale, the quake’s epicenter lay near La Pitaloza, just 12.6 kilometers beneath the surface. The tremor arrived with the force of a sudden, unseen hand, jolting the nation and setting off a cascade of aftershocks—more than forty in total—that kept residents on edge.

The depth of 12.6 kilometers amplified the shaking felt across a broad swath of the country. Six provinces reported power grid failures, leaving many without electricity. The outage was not merely a technical inconvenience; it forced the suspension of essential public services, including the metro system and airport operations. Yet, amid the chaos, the Panama Canal—an artery of global trade—remained operational, a small but significant sign of resilience.

While the 7.7-magnitude event wrought widespread structural damage, a separate 7.2-magnitude quake earlier in the week added to the toll. That tremor, centered 39 kilometers northwest of Tonosi, injured at least 27 people and damaged more than 400 buildings. Among the structures hit were 118 educational centers, a stark reminder that the quake’s impact reached beyond homes and businesses into the very places where Panama’s future is taught. The combined effect of the quakes left a patchwork of cracked walls, collapsed roofs, and damaged roads across the affected regions.
## The Canal Holds, the Nation Reacts

Even as the ground shook, the Panama Canal continued to function, underscoring the canal’s critical role in both national and international logistics. On the same day as the 7.7-magnitude quake, he declared the situation a national disaster, invoking emergency powers to mobilize resources and coordinate relief efforts. The declaration signaled both the severity of the event and the government’s readiness to act.

In the quake’s aftermath, emergency services poured onto the streets, conducting damage assessments. The initial reports indicated no fatalities from the 7.7-magnitude event, a fact that offered a glimmer of relief amid the devastation. However, the sheer scale of property damage—ranging from residential homes to schools—required a coordinated response. Agencies such as Sinaproc documented the extensive damage to infrastructure, reinforcing the need for a sustained recovery plan.

As Panama grapples with the immediate challenges—restoring power to six provinces, repairing the metro and airport, and rebuilding over 400 damaged structures—the longer-term picture begins to emerge.

The path to full recovery will be extensive. Yet the continued operation of the Panama Canal offers a symbolic and practical lifeline, reminding Panamanians that even in the wake of a powerful quake, the country’s most vital arteries can stay open.
